correctness.rationale: González-Riquelme and Oliveira e Silva, arXiv:2405.16647, Theorem 1.3 and §6, prove the sharp sixth-moment norm and necessity of constant modulus; the complete mathematical text of the relevant statement and proof was examined. For a constant-modulus maximizer, Fourier triple-convolution orthogonality has exactly the factor \(p^{-4}\); every fiberwise triangle inequality must attain equality because the constant function does so on each fiber. The translated equal-sums/equal-squares triples force \(z_t z_{t+3}^{2}=z_{t+1}^{2}z_{t+4}\) for every residue \(t\). The third multiplicative difference \(w_t\) consequently satisfies \(w_tw_{t+1}=1\). Odd cyclic length implies it is a constant sign, and telescoping products eliminate the negative sign. Therefore \(z_t=z_0\alpha^t\beta^{t(t-1)/2}\), with \(\alpha^p=\beta^p=1\); these are precisely scalar quadratic characters. Modulation shifts the target Fourier coordinates, proving sufficiency, and degree-two polynomial root counting yields \(p^2\) distinct projective classes. The exact finite-prime checker confirms fiber energies and character alignment for seven primes; these finite checks are not used to prove the infinite-prime theorem.

originality.rationale: The complete optimizer equality set is neither stated nor implied by the cited sharp-norm theorem alone: Theorem 1.3 of arXiv:2405.16647 establishes only constant modulus. An explicit cubic Prouhet-type collision and multiplicative finite differences prove phase necessity. The closest fully inspected moment-curve endpoint results cover L4 on the 2D parabola or L6 on the 3D cubic moment curve, not this L6 geometry. No equivalent published exact phase classification appeared in the named searches; residual prior-equivalence risk remains.
